#2604 -- the source behind the measurement

Produced by `python measure-2604.py --source`, run from a checkout of
the repo this file lives in. Every command is echoed exactly as
executed; re-run any of them yourself.

Probes 6 and 7 are ABSENCE claims. Each is preceded by a
known-positive CONTROL: the same pattern and the same tool, over a
scope where it is known to match. Without that, an empty result is
indistinguishable from a typo, a bad path filter, or a tool that
quietly declines to search -- which is a mistake this workflow has
made before.

========================================================================
1. -Fc carries DriverOption and NOT CoreOption -- so dxc.exe sees it and
   the library does not.
========================================================================

[exit] 0

4. What an unrecognised option does: it lands in OPT_UNKNOWN, and unless
   -Qunused-arguments is present, ReadDxcOpts fails the whole parse.
========================================================================

========================================================================
5. ...and -Qunused-arguments IS a CoreOption, which is why it is available
   to the library and can switch the failure off.
========================================================================

========================================================================
6. ABSENCE: opts.AssemblyCode -- the field -Fc feeds -- has no consumer
   anywhere inside dxcompiler/. Only the driver and a test tool act on
   it (the third hit, HLSLOptions.cpp:1336, only rejects a non-empty
   AssemblyCode when Metal codegen is on). This is why adding CoreOption
   to -Fc would not, on its own, implement the feature: nothing in the
   library would then act on the value.
========================================================================

this listing is also the complete set of readers):

========================================================================
8. Where E_INVALIDARG is manufactured, and why the CALL still returns
   S_OK: dxcutil::ReadOptsAndValidate builds an already-finished
   DxcResult carrying E_INVALIDARG and sets finished=true; Compile then
   hands that result back and returns S_OK. The failure is on the result
   object, not on the call -- a caller that only checks the HRESULT of
   Compile() sees success.
========================================================================

$ git grep -n -B 6 -A 10 "E_INVALIDARG, DXC_OUT_NONE" -- tools/clang/tools/dxcompiler/dxcutil.cpp
[exit] 0

========================================================================
9. ...and both compile entry points do exactly that: DxcCompiler::Compile
   (IDxcCompiler3, line ~562) and DxcCompilerAdapter::WrapCompile (the
   legacy IDxcCompiler, line ~1908). Both `return S_OK` with the failed
   result. This is why the harness reports call= and status= separately.
========================================================================

========================================================================
10. The documentation the 2020 comment relied on. docs/SPIR-V.rst says
    the listed options 'are also recognized by the library API calls',
    and -Fc is on that list. The measurement says otherwise -- see the
    c1-spirv-* rows in manual-case-release-history.txt. This is a real
    documentation defect and it is a sufficient explanation for the
    2020 reporter's surprise.
========================================================================

CONTROL (a sibling entry in the same list, to show the list is being searched):
$ git grep -c -E ``-Fo`` -- docs/SPIR-V.rst
[exit] 0
docs/SPIR-V.rst:1

CLAIM:
$ git grep -n -E "also recognized by the library|``-Fc``" -- docs/SPIR-V.rst
[exit] 0
docs/SPIR-V.rst:4198:also recognized by the library API calls.
docs/SPIR-V.rst:4211:- ``-Fc``: outputs SPIR-V disassembly to the given file

========================================================================
11. ...and that documentation has said so since before the issue was
    filed: the -Fc bullet since 2017, the 'also recognized' sentence
    since 2018. The issue is from 2019-11 and the comment from 2020-07.
========================================================================
